designFindings: The personal pay path and executePrepared are two separate implementations of prepare, check, sign and submit, and they give different guarantees. The personal path fences the auth lifetime only around a settled replay. Its abandon is unfenced, its submit is unfenced, and it reads the session twice. The command path fences every await, including abandon and submit. Evidence: execution.ts:180-275 vs command-execution.ts:80-256; prepared-execution.ts:16 vs :81.

The personal path calls abandon even when the prepare returned a settled replay and the caller then aborts. executePrepared never closes a replayed execution. Evidence: execution.ts:209-219 vs command-execution.ts:121.
A failed abandon call replaces the caller's real error (signer refusal, mismatch, cancel) with the abandon's own error. Evidence: prepared-execution.ts:32, :115.

One caller's onPrepared that throws fails a submission shared by every caller with the same request key, and the prepared execution is left open. Evidence: personal-flights.ts:84; execution.ts:221; command-execution.ts:208.

Lifecycle retries (personal and Organization) pass closePaymentOnExit false. A mismatch, an abort or a signer refusal leaves the prepared retry execution open on the backend. Evidence: lifecycle-execution.ts:120.

The budget-route check reads two other concepts' rows from the client (permissions.allowances.list, payroll.departments.get) and swallows any read failure as 'not bound'. On the Organization path a transient read error permanently abandons the Payment as prepared_mismatch. The reads also bypass the abort signal and the method span. Evidence: budget-route.ts:29-46; command-execution.ts:180-187.

Span names drift from the declared operation tree. Organization pay and payBatch open organizationPayments.pay and .payBatch, while org.payments.pay and org.payments.payBatch are declared and unused. personal payments.pay opens no span at all, so its prepare, submit and abandon carry no client trace. payments.pay appears only as a CANCELLED label. Evidence: organization-payments.ts:127,147; observability operations/org.ts:147-148, money.ts:17-18; methods.ts:65; result-bridge.ts:100-135.

Invocation controls are handled differently per method. Personal pay ignores correlation_id, journey_id, timeoutMs and deadlineMs. Organization methods strip the time limits (observationOnlyControls), so they bound only a restoring session read. A caller that joins a shared flight loses its own controls. Evidence: methods.ts:65 vs :66-69; capxul-effect.ts:19-29; organization-flights.ts:130-145.

Each step has its own error vocabulary. A missing signer is INVALID_INPUT on personal pay but NOT_IMPLEMENTED on retry and on the Organization path. Cancel errors name three different operations: payments, payments.pay and organization-pay(-batch). Evidence: execution.ts:189-190; lifecycle-methods.ts:16-17; organization-flights.ts:83-88; command-execution.ts:95; organization-flights.ts:79.

The two pay paths compute request keys differently. The personal path names its key slot by the raw input, the Organization path by the decoded intent. A caller-supplied key bypasses Web Locks and storage entirely (no-op finish). Flights live in one in-memory bundle, so a second tab or process can still prepare twice for the same key. Evidence: personal-pay.ts:79-83; organization-payment-requests.ts:211-215; request-keys.ts:73-74; personal-pay.ts:163; organization-payments.ts:34.
Personal subscribe does not validate the paymentId; the Organization path does. Evidence: methods.ts:52-64 vs organization-payment-reads.ts:124-129.

The SDK payments surface and the old book do not match. The CLI's payment send, retry, cancel and reschedule all go through client.approvals.prepare. So client.payments.pay and .retry and client.org(orgId).payments.pay, .payBatch and .retry are not used by the CLI. Meanwhile the book names client.payments.cancel and .reschedule, which do not exist. Evidence: apps/cli/src/commands/payment (5 client.approvals.prepare calls); apps/docs/factory/operations/payment.cancel.yaml:41, payment.reschedule.yaml:37; methods.ts:28-44.
